Pattern D (DD-Month-YYYY slug). Added use_target_url:true so the goto

operator_notes_2026_08_10: SUPERSEDES the 08-09 fix above — the 08-09 fix only patched the goto
step; the download step still had a hardcoded stale 'url' +
use_captured_url:true (which returns that literal URL unmodified,
ignoring target_date entirely — see _resolve_download_candidates), so
every harvest still fell through to the 28 June PDF as a last resort
and correctly got caught as stale downstream, but wastefully so.
Root cause of the date-guessing itself: this parish's filename
convention isn't stable — some weeks it's 'Newsletter-D-Month-YYYY-1.pdf'
(matches the evidence-file example), other weeks it's plain
'D-Month-YYYY.pdf' with no prefix/suffix (confirmed 2026-08-10: the
guessed .../08/Newsletter-9-August-2026-1.pdf 404s, but the real file
that week is .../08/9-August-2026.pdf) — no single date-rewrite pattern
covers both.
REAL FIX: bellaghyparish.com/current-newsletter/ is a WordPress redirect
page that 302s straight to whatever file is this week's actual
newsletter, whatever its name — no date-guessing needed at all. Chromium
aborts page.goto() on that redirect (ERR_ABORTED, ends on about:blank)
because it hands the response straight to the download manager instead
of rendering it; this was previously misreported as 'recipe replay
failed' for any goto step (not just click steps) pointed at a
redirect-to-download URL — fixed generically in _goto_or_download to
catch ERR_ABORTED and use the already-captured download, matching the
existing click-step handling in _click_locator_match.
